questions.title: Why does FlashAttention‑2 achieve only ~35% hardware utilization on H100 GPUs?
questions.question_body: The paper states that FlashAttention‑2 reaches only about 35 % utilization on the Hopper H100 GPU while optimized GEMM kernels achieve 80–90 %. I understood that FlashAttention‑2 already eliminates intermediate global memory writes/reads by fusing all operations into a single kernel. What architectural or algorithmic factors prevent higher occupancy/utilization on H100? Is it mainly due to not using Hopper‑specific Tensor Core instructions, or are there deeper reasons related to the synchronous execution model?

questions.title: How does producer‑consumer asynchrony via warp‑specialization work in FlashAttention‑3?
questions.question_body: Section 3 describes a "producer‑consumer" scheme where some warps act as producers (issuing TMA loads) and others act as consumers (performing WGMMA GEMMs). I am confused about how the warps are split, how data movement and computation are synchronized, and what role the circular SMEM buffer plays. Could someone walk through a concrete example of a CTA where warp 0 loads Q tiles while warp 1 computes the first GEMM, highlighting where barriers are placed?

questions.title: What is the “s‑stage circular SMEM buffer” used in the algorithm?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 mentions initializing a pipeline object to manage barrier synchronization with an "s‑stage circular SMEM buffer". How is this buffer organized across stages, what does the parameter s represent, and how does it enable overlapping loads of K/V tiles with computation? Also, why is a circular buffer preferred over a linear queue in this context?

questions.title: How does ping‑pong scheduling overlap softmax with GEMM across warp groups?
questions.question_body: The authors propose "ping‑pong" scheduling where warp group 1 computes softmax while warp group 2 performs GEMMs, then they swap roles. I am unsure how the `bar.sync` instructions enforce this ordering without causing deadlocks or excessive stalls. Can anyone provide a timeline diagram or step‑by‑step description showing which operations (softmax exponentials, row max reductions, WGMMA) run concurrently on the two warp groups?

questions.title: Why does exponential throughput become a bottleneck despite its lower FLOP count?
questions.question_body: "The H100 has 989 TFLOPS of FP16 matmul but only 3.9 TFLOPS of special functions such as exponential" – given that softmax involves far fewer FLOPs than the matmul (e.g., 512× less), why can exponentials still dominate half of the execution cycles? How does the difference between FLOP count and unit throughput lead to this situation, especially when moving from FP16 to FP8 where matmul throughput doubles but exponential throughput stays constant?

questions.title: What are WGMMA instructions and how do they differ from earlier HMMA/Tensor Core calls?
questions.question_body: "WGMMA" stands for warp‑group‑wide matrix multiply‑accumulate introduced in Hopper. How does its programming model differ from the older `hmma`/`mma` intrinsics used on Ampere? In particular, what changes are required in kernel code to switch from HMMA to WGMMA, and how does WGMMA enable asynchronous execution?

questions.title: What exactly does “k‑major” layout mean for FP8 WGMMA operands?
questions.question_body: Section 2 mentions that FP8 WGMMA only accepts k‑major operand layout (contiguous in the inner K dimension). Could someone define k‑major versus mn‑major layout formally, perhaps with an example tensor shape (e.g., $N\times d$) and memory stride ordering? Why is this restriction present only for FP8 and not for FP16?
